quests.instruction: Mina grabs the last red marker just before Tara reaches it. Tara folds her arms and says loudly, 'I was about to take it!' Which feeling fits Tara best?
quests.correctAnswer: Frustrated 😤
options: Delighted 😄
Peaceful 🕊️
Frustrated 😤
quests.hint: Look at the folded arms and the loud voice, and think about what she wanted to do.
quests.explanation: Tara wanted the marker and was beaten to it by a second. Her loud voice and folded arms show frustration, not delight or peace.
quests.funFact: Frustration often comes when a small plan is blocked, even by an accident.

quests.instruction: Imran and Sia both want to be goalkeeper for the match. What is a fair way to solve it?
quests.correctAnswer: Take turns in each half or draw lots 🥅
options: Let the biggest kid decide for everyone 💪
Whoever shouts loudest gets the spot 📢
Take turns in each half or draw lots 🥅
quests.hint: Which solution gives each child an equal chance?
quests.explanation: Turns or drawing lots give both children the same chance. Shouting or deciding by size rewards force, not fairness.
quests.funFact: Drawing lots has been used for centuries to settle fair choices.

quests.instruction: Hiro told his friend a private secret. A day later two classmates teased him about it. Which feeling fits Hiro best?
quests.correctAnswer: Hurt 💔
options: Curious 🤔
Hurt 💔
Proud 😌
quests.hint: Think about what happens to trust when a secret is shared.
quests.explanation: A shared secret turned into teasing shows that trust was broken, which brings hurt. The feeling points to how much the friendship mattered.
quests.funFact: Trust builds slowly, and it can be repaired with honesty and time.

quests.instruction: Aarav realizes he just cut Lena off in the middle of her idea. What should he say?
quests.correctAnswer: Sorry, I interrupted. Please go ahead. 🙇
options: It is the same thing I was going to say. 🙄
You were taking too long, anyway. ⏳
Sorry, I interrupted. Please go ahead. 🙇
quests.hint: Which sentence gives the floor back to Lena?
quests.explanation: Naming the interruption and inviting her to continue repairs it quickly. Blaming her length or claiming the idea shows disrespect.
quests.funFact: Quick apologies for small interruptions keep a conversation friendly.

quests.instruction: Gia asks to borrow Pat's brand-new art set. Pat hesitates and holds the box close. Which feeling might Pat have?
quests.correctAnswer: Worried 😟
options: Delighted 😄
Worried 😟
Bored 😑
quests.hint: Think about why someone might hold a new thing so tightly.
quests.explanation: Holding a new item close and hesitating suggests Pat is worried about it getting damaged or lost. It does not mean Pat is selfish.
quests.funFact: Feeling protective of new things is common. Talking about the worry can help.

quests.instruction: Pat wants to share but is worried about the art set. Which sentence helps both children?
quests.correctAnswer: I am worried it will break. Can we use it together at my desk? 🎨
options: I am worried it will break. Can we use it together at my desk? 🎨
Sure, take it home, because I do not care what happens to it. 😔
No, because you always break everything that I ever lend to you. 🚫
quests.hint: Which sentence says the worry and offers an idea?
quests.explanation: Sharing the worry honestly and suggesting a safe way to share solves the problem for both children. Refusing with blame or giving in without caring does not.
quests.funFact: Using something together can be a good way to share when you are not ready to lend.

quests.instruction: Raj thinks it is unfair that one player skips the laps everyone else must run. What is the most helpful thing for Raj to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask the coach calmly about the rule after practice 🧑‍🏫
options: Ask the coach calmly about the rule after practice 🧑‍🏫
Complain loudly about the rule to all of the other teammates 📢
Refuse to run any laps and sit down on the field in protest 🪑
quests.hint: Which choice gets his concern to the person who can answer it?
quests.explanation: A calm question to the coach after practice raises the concern in the right place at a good time. Protesting or complaining to teammates does not fix it.
quests.funFact: Coaches usually have reasons, and a calm question lets them explain.

quests.instruction: Kavita studied for two weeks and got a top mark. A classmate says, 'You are just lucky,' and Kavita bites her lip hard. What feeling is this?
quests.correctAnswer: Hurt 💔
options: Hurt 💔
Thrilled 🥳
Curious 🤔
quests.hint: Think about how it feels when someone ignores your effort.
quests.explanation: Her effort was brushed off as luck, and the lip-biting shows she is holding back a hurt feeling.
quests.funFact: Telling someone, 'I worked hard for this,' can help them see your effort.

quests.instruction: You accidentally knock a friend's drawing off her desk and it tears. Which apology is best?
quests.correctAnswer: I am sorry. I will help you fix it. 🩹
options: It was only paper, so it is not a big deal. 📄
It is your fault for putting it so near the edge. 👉
I am sorry. I will help you fix it. 🩹
quests.hint: Which apology takes responsibility and offers to repair?
quests.explanation: A real apology owns the mistake and offers to help fix it. Minimizing the damage or blaming her does not show care.
quests.funFact: Offering to repair something is a strong way to show that you mean your apology.

quests.instruction: Aisha waves at Jen across the hall and Jen does not wave back. Aisha wonders whether Jen is ignoring her. What should Aisha do first?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask Jen if she saw her before deciding anything ❓
options: Tell all the other kids that Jen is rude to her 📢
Ignore Jen completely for the rest of the school day 🚫
Ask Jen if she saw her before deciding anything ❓
quests.hint: Which choice checks the facts before reacting?
quests.explanation: Asking first checks whether it was a mix-up. Jen may have simply not seen the wave. Many conflicts begin with a guess.
quests.funFact: Many arguments start with a guess about what another person was thinking.

quests.instruction: After the argument, Tom stares at his shoes with heavy shoulders. He wants to say sorry but does not know how. What feeling is behind this?
quests.correctAnswer: Regretful 🥀
options: Regretful 🥀
Proud 😌
Excited 🤩
quests.hint: Think about wishing you could take something back.
quests.explanation: Wanting to say sorry and not knowing how shows he regrets what happened. It is a feeling that can lead to repair.
quests.funFact: Writing a short note can be an easier way to start an apology.

quests.instruction: Mia keeps rolling the dice twice in a board game. Sam thinks it is unfair. What is the best thing for Sam to say?
quests.correctAnswer: I think it is my turn. Can we check the rules together? 🎲
options: Never mind, I will stop playing the game now and sit alone. 🪑
I think it is my turn. Can we check the rules together? 🎲
I will just grab the dice and roll whenever I feel like it. 🤚
quests.hint: Which sentence raises the problem and invites a fair check?
quests.explanation: Calmly pointing to the turn and suggesting a rule check solves the problem without a fight. Sulking or grabbing makes it worse.
quests.funFact: Reading the rules together settles many game arguments.

quests.instruction: Kai watches his group laugh and walk off without telling him where they are going. What could Kai do?
quests.correctAnswer: Say, 'I felt left out. Can I come next time?' 🙋
options: Follow them silently and glare at everyone 👀
Say, 'I felt left out. Can I come next time?' 🙋
Spread a rumor about the group to get back 📢
quests.hint: Which response tells them how he feels and asks for a change?
quests.explanation: Telling them how it felt and asking to join next time gives them a chance to include him. Glaring or rumors make things worse.
quests.funFact: Sometimes a group does not realize someone feels left out until they are told.

quests.instruction: Nori realizes the group left Kai out and her tummy feels heavy. Which feeling fits Nori?
quests.correctAnswer: Guilty 😓
options: Bored 😑
Guilty 😓
Proud 😌
quests.hint: Think about the feeling after we notice we hurt someone.
quests.explanation: A heavy tummy after leaving someone out shows guilt. It is an uncomfortable feeling that points us toward making things right.
quests.funFact: Noticing a guilty feeling can help us fix a mistake before it grows.

quests.instruction: Nori wants to fix it. What is the best first step?
quests.correctAnswer: Find Kai, say sorry for leaving him out, and invite him now 🤝
options: Find Kai, say sorry for leaving him out, and invite him now 🤝
Tell Kai that it was his own fault for not asking to join in 👉
Wait and hope that the whole thing goes away by itself soon ⏳
quests.hint: Which step takes responsibility and includes him right away?
quests.explanation: Apologizing and inviting him right away repairs the hurt. Waiting or blaming leaves it unresolved.
quests.funFact: A quick invitation can change someone's whole day.

quests.instruction: Pranav and Ana disagree about how to build a bridge. Each insists that their way is best. What is a constructive step?
quests.correctAnswer: Try each idea quickly and see which holds more weight 🌉
options: Try each idea quickly and see which holds more weight 🌉
Let one of them build alone while the other just watches 🚶
Argue loudly until one of them finally gives up and agrees 🗯️
quests.hint: Which choice uses both ideas instead of a fight?
quests.explanation: Testing both ideas lets the bridge decide, not the loudest voice. Both children feel included.
quests.funFact: Engineers test several designs before choosing the strongest one.

quests.instruction: The group picks Gaurav's design. Ana says, 'Okay,' very quietly and looks at her sketch. Which feeling fits Ana?
quests.correctAnswer: Disappointed 😞
options: Peaceful 🕊️
Disappointed 😞
Excited 🤩
quests.hint: Look at her quiet voice and where she is looking.
quests.explanation: A quiet 'Okay' and a long look at her own sketch show disappointment that her idea was not chosen.
quests.funFact: Being disappointed about a decision does not mean you are a bad sport.

quests.instruction: Two friends disagree about which music to play. Which statement is a good compromise?
quests.correctAnswer: We could play your song first and then mine 🎵
options: We will play only mine because I am right 🏆
Do whatever you want, I am leaving 🚶
We could play your song first and then mine 🎵
quests.hint: Which statement gives both of them something?
quests.explanation: A compromise gives each person part of what they want. Insisting or leaving ends the conversation.
quests.funFact: Compromise works best when both people feel they have gained something.

quests.instruction: Jo thinks it is unfair that his little sister gets extra tablet time. What could he say to a parent?
quests.correctAnswer: It feels unfair to me that Rani gets more time. Can we talk about the rule? ⚖️
options: You obviously like her a lot more than you like me, and you always have! 💔
I hate this whole family and I am never coming out of my room again, ever. 🚪
It feels unfair to me that Rani gets more time. Can we talk about the rule? ⚖️
quests.hint: Which sentence names his feeling and asks to talk about the rule?
quests.explanation: Saying how it feels and asking to talk about the rule opens a fair conversation. Accusations or running away do not.
quests.funFact: A parent can often explain a rule better when they know how it feels to you.

quests.instruction: Jonas says a sincere sorry and offers to redo the poster. Mira lets out a breath and her shoulders loosen. Which feeling fits Mira?
quests.correctAnswer: Relieved 😅
options: Relieved 😅
Bored 😑
Furious 😡
quests.hint: Look at her breath and her shoulders.
quests.explanation: A breath out and loosened shoulders show that tension is leaving, which is relief. A sincere apology can do that.
quests.funFact: Hearing a real apology can lift a heavy feeling.

quests.instruction: You disagree with a friend's idea for a skit. Which sentence is a respectful way to say so?
quests.correctAnswer: I see it differently. Can I explain my idea? 💬
options: That is a dumb idea, nobody will like it. 👎
I see it differently. Can I explain my idea? 💬
Fine, you win, whatever you want. 🙄
quests.hint: Which sentence disagrees without putting the other person down?
quests.explanation: Saying 'I see it differently' and asking to explain disagrees respectfully. Insulting or giving in with sarcasm does not help.
quests.funFact: Good ideas often come from combining two different views.

quests.instruction: Someone says a friend said something mean about you, but you cannot be sure it is true. What is the best first step?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask the friend directly or ask a trusted adult for help 🙋
options: Believe it right away and stop talking to that friend 🚫
Ask the friend directly or ask a trusted adult for help 🙋
Say something mean about the friend to everyone in return 📢
quests.hint: Which step finds out what really happened?
quests.explanation: Checking with the friend or with an adult looks for the facts before reacting. Rumors can twist what was said.
quests.funFact: Messages passed from person to person often change along the way.

quests.instruction: Sana accused her friend of leaving her out, then learned the friend had saved her a seat. Her cheeks burn. Which feeling fits Sana?
quests.correctAnswer: Embarrassed 😳
options: Embarrassed 😳
Furious 😡
Proud 😌
quests.hint: Think about discovering she was wrong in front of someone.
quests.explanation: Learning that she jumped to a wrong conclusion made her cheeks burn. Embarrassment is normal after a mix-up, and it can be repaired.
quests.funFact: Everyone jumps to a wrong conclusion sometimes. What matters is how we fix it.

quests.instruction: Sana wants to make things right. Which words would help most?
quests.correctAnswer: I jumped to conclusions. I am sorry. Thanks for saving my seat. 🤝
options: Let us just forget the whole thing and move on. 🙈
You should have told me earlier, then none of this happens. 👉
I jumped to conclusions. I am sorry. Thanks for saving my seat. 🤝
quests.hint: Which words take responsibility and notice the kindness?
quests.explanation: She owns the mistake, apologizes, and thanks her friend. That repairs trust.
quests.funFact: A thank-you can be part of an apology when someone was kind to you.

quests.instruction: Your group makes plans in a chat you are not part of. What is a good step?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell one of them how you feel and ask to be added 📱
options: Block everyone in the group and delete all the messages 🚫
Make a new chat of her own and leave them out too 🔄
Tell one of them how you feel and ask to be added 📱
quests.hint: Which step puts the feeling into words and asks for something to change?
quests.explanation: Telling someone how you feel and asking to be added gives them a chance to fix it. Blocking or leaving them out turns the hurt into a fight.
quests.funFact: Groups sometimes forget to include people by accident.

quests.instruction: Two of your friends are arguing and each asks you to pick a side. Which feeling might you have?
quests.correctAnswer: Uneasy 😧
options: Bored 😑
Delighted 😄
Uneasy 😧
quests.hint: Think about being pulled in two directions.
quests.explanation: Being asked to pick between two people you care about is uncomfortable, which fits uneasy. It is a normal reaction to loyalty pressure.
quests.funFact: Being in the middle of a friends' argument is hard for almost anyone.

quests.instruction: You are asked to pick a side between two friends. What is a kind way to answer?
quests.correctAnswer: I care about you both. I will not pick a side, but I can listen. 💛
options: I care about you both. I will not pick a side, but I can listen. 💛
Do not ever talk to me about this again, because I am done. 🚫
I will just pick whichever one of you is more popular at school. ⭐
quests.hint: Which answer protects both friendships?
quests.explanation: Saying you care about both and offering to listen keeps you kind and fair. Choosing by popularity or shutting people out hurts them.
quests.funFact: You can care about two people who are not getting along.

quests.instruction: Voices start to rise in a disagreement. Which step should come first?
quests.correctAnswer: Pause and take a breath ⏸️
options: Pause and take a breath ⏸️
Call other people to join your side 📣
Say the most hurtful thing you can think of 💥
quests.hint: Think about what gives you a chance to choose a better action.
quests.explanation: A pause gives you time to calm down and choose helpful words. Hurtful words and recruiting others make the conflict bigger.
quests.funFact: A quick breath can make the difference between a fight and a conversation.

quests.instruction: Aiden apologized, but Lia still feels hurt. Which response is the most respectful?
quests.correctAnswer: Lia says she needs time, and Aiden says he understands 🕰️
options: Aiden says that he will never apologize to Lia ever again 🚫
Lia says she needs time, and Aiden says he understands 🕰️
Aiden demands that Lia forgive him right now, since he said sorry 📢
quests.hint: Which response respects Lia's feelings and time?
quests.explanation: Giving someone time after an apology respects their feelings. Forgiveness cannot be forced.
quests.funFact: Forgiveness often takes time, and that is okay.

quests.instruction: What does it mean to repair a friendship after a fight?
quests.correctAnswer: Understanding what happened, saying sorry, and making a plan to do better 🧩
options: Deciding who was completely right and who was completely wrong in the fight ⚖️
Understanding what happened, saying sorry, and making a plan to do better 🧩
Pretending that nothing ever happened and never talking about it with anyone 🙈
quests.hint: Think about what makes a friendship stronger afterward.
quests.explanation: Repair means understanding, apologizing, and agreeing on what to do next. Pretending or deciding blame does not rebuild trust.
quests.funFact: Friendships that survive an argument can end up closer than before.
